question: Do intentional walks gain win probability for the defense?
answer: Mostly no. With a runner on 2nd and 1 out, the IBB costs the defense 2.0 points of win probability. In the other states there is no gain I can tell apart from 0.
findings: Runner on 2nd, 1 out: -2.0 points (CI -3.3 to -0.7), n=545 IBB. Late and close it is -4.1 points (CI -7.1 to -1.2).
2nd and 3rd, 1 out: +1.3 points (CI +0.9 to +1.8) over the PA, but +0.3 (CI -0.8 to +1.4) to the end of the inning.
IBB batters are +15 points of season wOBA over the other batters in these states, which is in the model.
IBB per season: 826 in 2016 and 393 in 2025 (non-pitcher batters, innings 1-9).
method: The change in empirical WE from the defense's view, from the start of the PA to the end of the half-inning (main) and over the PA. An OLS with batter and on-deck season wOBA and inning x score x season cells, with SE clustered by game. The comparison is pitching to the batter in the same state.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 6,129 intentional walks to non-pitchers in innings 1-9. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: Runner on 2nd, 1 out: -2.0 points in 2015-19 and -1.9 in 2020-25 (SE 0.8, 1.2).
